motion.name: rule-draw

motion.name: album-snap
motion.purpose: Album track paging.

motion.name: picker-open

motion.purpose: Cover-picker panel open and close.

motion.name: card-in
motion.purpose: Next challenge item arrives.

motion.name: card-fly
motion.purpose: Correctly sorted item leaves.

motion.name: card-shake
motion.purpose: Wrong answer on the card and the chosen bin.

motion.name: way-pulse
motion.purpose: Marks the way card chosen by "Quero ajudar com".

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

motion.name: diploma-in
motion.value: .9s ease-out: from translateY(-60px) rotate(-7deg) scale(.86), overshoot, settle at -0.6deg
motion.purpose: The diploma lands on the page when the round ends.

motion.name: score-count
motion.purpose: The score in the diploma sentence counts up.

motion.name: star-pop
motion.purpose: Stars appear one by one.

motion.name: seal-in
motion.purpose: The red seal stamps the diploma.

motion.name: cap-fall
motion.value: 1.4–2.6s, 34 caps at >=75% right, 14 otherwise, cover cap colours
motion.purpose: Bottle-cap confetti over the diploma.

motion.name: scroll-reveal
motion.value: rise 22px / pinned photos drop 22px with -5deg tilt, .7–.8s, 70ms stagger (max 6)
motion.purpose: Content enters as you scroll; never hidden at rest; first on-screen batch stays still.

motion.name: hero-in
motion.value: headline, lede, CTAs rise 16px at 0/.15/.28s; hero photo pins in
motion.purpose: Page open.

motion.name: count-up
motion.purpose: Latest-result and booklet figures count to their value.

motion.name: cap-float
motion.purpose: Loose caps on the cover drift.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Buttons, chips, bins, level pills when pressed.

motion.name: view-transition
motion.value: old .22s fade up, new .32s rise; nav fixed
motion.purpose: Between pages where supported.

motion.name: smooth-scroll
motion.value: Lenis 1.3.26 self-hosted, lerp .1, fine pointer only, anchors offset nav+12px
motion.purpose: Inertial wheel/trackpad scrolling; native on touch; off under reduced motion.

motion.name: photo-develop
motion.value: clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0)→0 .9s + filter saturate(.2) brightness(1.35) contrast(.85)→none 1.6s
motion.purpose: Photos reveal like developing polaroids as they enter; content photos only.

challenge.name: O desafio das tampinhas / The bottle-cap challenge
challenge.rotation: freshness: items seen longest ago (or never) first, from localStorage ficha-vistos; consecutive rounds share at most the single cork item; all 26 appear within three rounds
challenge.instruction: centred handwritten line above the bins: 'Clica na categoria que achas correta:' / 'Click the category you think is right:'
challenge.timer: from the first card to the last answer; shown in the diploma sentence and PNG; breaks ties on the wall
challenge.reveal: diploma hidden until the round ends (.diploma[hidden] must beat its grid display); drop-in, score count-up, stars pop, seal stamps, cap confetti; none under reduced motion
challenge.reward: Diploma de Amigo do Martim; PNG 1600x1130 named 'Diploma Amigo do Martim - <nome>.png', navigator.share with file where supported, else download
challenge.wall: opt-in checkbox on the diploma (unticked by default); saving or sharing sends the result once
challenge.highlight: worksheet tinted by cover: 50% cover + white on light covers, 12% cover over #E9F0FF on dark covers; cover glow and ring; card, bins and idle level pills stay white
challenge.order: name, level (in head, above rule), Onde vai isto? + card, instruction, bins, progress dots + score centred, feedback

share.order: native (only if navigator.share) first, then WhatsApp, Facebook, X, TikTok, copy link; compact on-cover variant = native + WhatsApp + Facebook + TikTok
share.style: white pills, 2px ink, monochrome ink SVG icons; hover highlighter; never network brand colours
share.tiktok: no web share link: copies text + link and opens tiktok.com/upload; on the diploma, hands the PNG to the share sheet (or downloads it) with caption and hashtags copied

images.loading: lazy by default; revealed album slides, thanks band and padel photo eager; remaining lazy images switched to eager after load in idle time (iOS Safari)

printables.container: the sheet's <figure> is the size container (container-type:inline-size), never the sheet itself
printables.printScope: print rules only on their own page (body:has(.cartaz-page), body.print-book); no global print CSS
printables.page: @page sheet{size:A4;margin:0} with .a4{page:sheet}; other pages keep default margins
printables.fit: one sheet = one A4 page; re-check overflow in PT, EN and a real PDF after any change
printables.typeFloor: poster and label body text in ink, never below 3cqw
printables.photos: no drop shadow in print (thin #C9CDD6 border)

wall.ranking: per level: most right, then fastest time, then earliest date; each first name + town counts once per level with its best result; top 10
wall.privacy: first name only (+ optional town); word block-list client and server; parents hide a row with 'x' in the sheet
wall.backend: Google Apps Script web app over a family Google Sheet (backend/LEIA-ME.md); rate limit 60/min; cache 60s
wall.offline: without MURAL_API_URL: js/mural.js + the visitor's own result, with a note saying so

map.library: Leaflet 1.9.4 (cdnjs) over OpenStreetMap tiles, slightly desaturated
map.markers: cap-shaped discs in the point-type colour: school #FF7A1A, community #12884A, health #E0301E, sport #2B5FA8, business #7A4FB0
map.nearest: geolocation only on tap, never leaves the browser; sorts the list and opens the closest

domain.hosting: DreamHost ams1-shared-02; GitHub Actions rsync on every push; .htaccess https + no-www + 404 + cache
domain.publish: sh tools/publish.sh, then commit and push site/

photoStack.controls: tap photo or 'toca para ver a próxima foto' with n/6 counter

narrative.overview:
The site is a Portuguese primary-school squared exercise book that Martim filled in himself. The page is bright white paper with a fine 24px grid tinted by the pen colour, and a red margin line. A cover takes over whole regions (the hero's left half, the VOLTA panel, the next-event card, the footer), with a handful of bottle caps scattered on it. The visitor chooses that cover from twelve, the way a child picks a notebook at the stationery shop. The default is night blue. His story reads as a composition. The BigBag money reads as a worked sum. Sorting caps is a challenge on a worksheet he corrects in red pen, and finishing it earns a friendship diploma. The events live in a photo album. Every visual device comes from the stationery of a Portuguese school desk: taped-in photos and polaroids, a name label on the cover, a spiral binding, highlighter marks, red ticks and circles, and a round "Muito bem!" stamp.

Density is generous and phone-first. Body type is large (18px) in a face built for low vision. Contrast is high: dark ink on white paper, and the cover's own text colour on each cover. Heavy compressed grotesque headings give the book a confident voice. Martim's own handwriting, in a dark pen, runs through the page as marginalia. The mood is cheerful, soft and not pitying: a child showing his homework and his team's photos, fist in the air.

The world rejects the charity default (full-bleed hero photo, progress bar and a lone Donate button). It also rejects the cream-paper-and-serif "warm family" look: the paper is cool white, and the type is sans and handwriting. After review it also rejects a single brand-primary cover, because a blue, yellow and red trio read as supermarket branding. The identity lives in the book's structure and the caps, not in one colour.
keyCharacteristics: Squared paper ground (24px grid tinted by the pen colour) with a red margin line on every paper section.
A visitor-chosen cover (12 options, night blue by default) as a region-owning surface, carrying its own text colour.
Bottle caps in four colours per cover, scattered on the cover and used as the nav tab underlines.
Stationery accents with fixed jobs: red pen marks, the highlighter for actions and marks, dark-pen handwriting.
One cover slot that everything themed reads from, derived in code from seven values per cover.
2px ink outlines on every card, table, chip and field, as if drawn with a ruler.
Objects laid on the page (photos, polaroid slides, label, stamp, caps) sit at slight angles and cast soft shadows.
Hand-drawn SVG pictograms with 2.5px ink strokes.
The family's original logo, recoloured per cover from the action colour; partner and supporter logos always sit on white chips.
The book also leaves the screen: an A4 poster with container labels and an 8-page booklet, drawn in the same world, print exactly as previewed in the chosen cover.

rules.name: The Cover Text Rule
rules.body: All text on a cover uses that cover's on-cover (headings, links, ghost buttons) or on-cover-soft (copy). Never hard-code white or ink on a cover. Red and red-ink never set text on a cover (3.1:1 and 2.35:1 on noite).

rules.name: The Highlighter Mark Rule
rules.body: On light covers and on paper, the highlighter is a background only: button fill, swipe, selection, play disc. It is never text (1.0–1.4:1 against light covers). On dark covers it doubles as hl-on-cover text. On dark covers the headline's marked phrase becomes a solid highlighter block with ink text.

rules.name: The Action Pair Rule
rules.body: Solid buttons use `--action` with `--action-ink`, never a fixed white. Any cover added to or edited in `PALETTES` must reach 4.5:1 for action-ink on action and for on-cover-soft and hl-on-cover on the cover. Red stays a marking colour and is never a button fill.

rules.name: The One Slot Rule
rules.body: Themed colour is always referenced through the cover variables, including inline SVG fills such as the brand mark and the loose caps, so any cover swaps the whole book at once. New themed tokens are derived in `applyPal()` from the seven cover values, never hard-coded per component.

rules.name: The Caps Are Caps Rule
rules.body: Cap colours (cap1–cap4 and the pictogram colours) only ever appear as caps or cap-shaped marks: the loose caps on the cover, pictograms, the 4px nav tab underlines, timetable dots and the dots on picker swatches. They never fill surfaces or set text.

rules.name: The Logo Follows the Action Rule
rules.body: The family's logo takes its colours only from `--logo-1/2/3`, which `applyPal()` derives from the cover's action and pen colours. Never recolour it by hand or give it a fixed brand colour.

rules.name: The Dark Lettering Rule
rules.body: On a light cover the logo's lettering is never white. The footer mark uses on-cover, so it goes dark on light covers and off-white only on dark ones.

rules.name: The White Chip Rule
rules.body: Partner and supporter logos always sit on a white chip (sheet white, 1.5px rule border, 5–10px radius), whether on paper, in a table or on a cover. They are never placed on the cover colour or the grid directly, and never recoloured, except for single-colour marks re-inked dark for legibility.

rules.name: The Diploma Paper Rule
rules.body: The diploma is the only cream surface in the system (#FFFDF7). It is a certificate handed out of the book, not a page in it. Everywhere else the paper stays cool white.

rules.name: The Two Reds Rule
rules.body: Red (#E0301E) is for strokes, fills and large display marks. Red-ink (#C21F0E) is for any text at body size, on paper. Don't swap them.

rules.name: The Martim's Pen Rule
rules.body: Gochi Hand appears only where Martim is writing: his notes, captions, the sum, filled-in values, corrections, feedback, the thank-you line, his signature, and short first-person prompts beside a control ("Quero ajudar com…", "Onde vai isto?", "Escolhe a capa", "Desafia os teus amigos:"), and names the visitor writes into the book (the challenge name field, the diploma name). It never sets headings, buttons' own labels, navigation, form labels or any instruction a reader must parse at length.

rules.name: The Heavy Compressed Rule
rules.body: Every heading, h1 to h3, and every display figure is Bricolage 800 at 84% width with negative tracking. There is no light or regular display weight in this world.

rules.name: The Tabular Sums Rule
rules.body: Numbers in sums, rates, totals and the album counter use tabular lining numerals, so columns line up like homework.

rules.name: The Taped-In Rule
rules.body: Only an object lying on or floating over the page casts a shadow, and it is always soft, low and warm or blue-black. No hard offset shadows, no glows, no shadow on flat panels or tables.

dos: Do keep every paper section on the 24px grid, with the red margin line set at clamp(20px, 6vw, 88px).
Do set all cover text in on-cover or on-cover-soft, whichever cover is active.
Do use the highlighter with ink text and an ink border for the primary action, and `--action` with `--action-ink` for solid buttons.
Do reference every themed colour through the cover variables, and derive new themed tokens in `applyPal()`.
Do check any cover added to or edited in `PALETTES` against 4.5:1 for on-cover-soft and hl-on-cover on the cover, action-ink on action and ink on hl before it enters the picker.
Do set every heading in Bricolage Grotesque 800 at font-stretch 84% with negative tracking.
Do keep reading copy at 1rem or larger in Atkinson Hyperlegible, and body copy at 1.125rem/1.6 with a 62ch measure.
Do outline cards, tables, chips and fields in 2px ink. Switch to a dashed border for optional or inactive states.
Do use red-ink (#C21F0E) for any red text at body size, on paper only.
Do frame photos as white-bordered prints with handwritten captions. Tape them in the book, but never in event contexts.
